subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What request-scoped dry-run security contract should OpenClaw expose for agent tool execution across CLI, Gateway or embedded runs, built-in tools, plugin tools, client tools, and hooks?
rationale: Current main lacks the feature, but adding it changes a security-sensitive runtime contract and the issue’s proposed process-global adapter flag is not clearly safe for concurrent or Gateway-owned execution.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify CLI and runtime semantics first, then implement a bounded core contract with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, and embedded paths.

options.title: Defer to broader workflow modes
options.body: Keep this blocked until the Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent mode design chooses shared vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Reject global dry-run
options.body: Continue using scoped command dry-runs, sandboxing, reader agents, and tool policy if maintainers decide a global preview boundary is too easy to misread as a sandbox guarantee.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify CLI and runtime semantics first, then implement a bounded core contract with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, and embedded paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal for the adapter/hook execution contract points to Peter’s before_tool_call integration work.
